import FreeCAD
import Part

# Create a new document
doc = FreeCAD.newDocument("BoxWithOffset")

# Create a box with dimensions 36x24x12, positioned at origin (0,0,0)
# Box is created centered at origin by default, so we need to position it
# The task requires lower-back-left corner at origin, spanning X=0-36, Y=0-24, Z=0-12

# Create a box primitive - Part.Box creates a box centered at origin
box_shape = Part.makeBox(36, 24, 12)

# Move the box so its lower-back-left corner is at origin
# By default, makeBox creates box from (-length/2, -width/2, -height/2) to (length/2, width/2, height/2)
# We need to translate by (+18, +12, +6) to move from center to origin corner
translation = FreeCAD.Vector(18, 12, 6)
box_shape.translate(translation)

# Create a Part object in the document
box_obj = doc.addObject("Part::Feature", "Box")
box_obj.Shape = box_shape

# Apply Part Offset with Mode=Skin, Join type=Tangent/Arc, Offset=2mm outward
# In FreeCAD, the offset operation uses the Part.Offset function
offset_shape = Part.Shape.offset(box_shape, 2.0, joinType=2, mode=1)
# joinType=2 corresponds to Tangent/Arc (0=Arc, 1=Miter, 2=Tangent)
# mode=1 corresponds to Skin mode (0=Default, 1=Skin, 2=Skeleton)

# Create the offset feature in the document
offset_obj = doc.addObject("Part::Feature", "OffsetShape")
offset_obj.Shape = offset_shape

# Recompute the document
doc.recompute()

# Save the document
doc.saveAs("/home/user/Unnamed.FCStd")

print("Document saved successfully!")
print(f"Box shape volume: {box_shape.Volume}")
print(f"Offset shape volume: {offset_shape.Volume}")

FreeCAD.closeDocument(doc.Name)
